insights.body: For All App, App Total Install in US is +0.7% while all countries together are -5.3% — a gap of +6.0pp. US is about 38% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -5.2% matches the new subs signed up 7 days earlier.
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 09-10 vs 09-03 is -5.2%, and App Total New Subs on 09-03 vs 08-27 was -7.4% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

insights.title: Best and worst markets — GB turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (20.6% vs 11.8% overall).
insights.body: In GB, 20.6% of installs turn into new subs, versus 11.8% across all markets and apps (+8.8pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. GB is about 4% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -20.8% this period.

insights.title: Market trend — MX is gaining ground fast on turning installs into subs (+27.1%, now 11.3%).
insights.body: In MX, 11.3% of installs now turn into new subs — +27.1% versus last period. It is about 3% of revenue (a market worth watching): more of the people downloading are subscribing, which should help revenue within a week or two.

insights.title: Next period outlook — No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -10.3% and App Total Install is -5.3%; the gap between them (-5.0pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.
